The '''Solaran-Khalindarian Conference of 1940''' was a wartime diplomatic conference held in [[Congrave]], [[Solara]], during the [[Avant Great War]]. It secured Khalindar's support against the [[Vesperan Empire]] and became the origin point of the later [[Khalindarian reparations dispute]].

The old Miraheze page title misspelled the event as "Confederence." The corrected title is "Conference."

== Background ==

By 1940, the [[United Alignment of Nations]] needed additional manpower, geography, and pressure against the Vesperan Empire. Khalindar was strategically positioned to tie down Vesperan forces but was unwilling to commit without major guarantees.

Solara viewed Khalindar as useful to the anti-Vesperan war effort. Khalindar viewed the war as an opportunity to secure territory, resources, and recognition that would expand imperial influence.

== Negotiations ==

The Solaran delegation was led by [[Alistair McGregor]] and Foreign Minister [[Eliza Harrington]]. Khalindar was represented by Emperor [[Mikael Khalindar II]] and General [[Fredrik Hagen]].

The agreement promised Khalindar territorial gains from Vesperan-held lands, favorable trade access, infrastructure investment in newly acquired areas, military aid, training, intelligence sharing, and logistical support.

== Postwar Dispute ==

The conference became controversial after the Vesperan defeat in 1949. Khalindar argued that its wartime sacrifices had been made on the basis of Solaran promises. Solara and other postwar decision-makers did not transfer the full promised settlement.

Old source material says some promised territories were instead absorbed into the Buda Republic and Belcanto Nations. Khalindar treated this as a breach of the 1940 agreement and repeatedly demanded reparations.

== Legacy ==

The 1940 conference turned a wartime bargain into a long-term diplomatic wound. For Solara, it was a successful wartime maneuver that helped weaken Vespera. For Khalindar, it became evidence that Solara had used the empire during the Great War and then ignored its claims afterward.
